title: SPK contributor vesting is claimable permissionlessly, so no party can withhold vested compensation
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.4.1 describes "a 4-year linear vesting schedule that compensates Spark contributors," and the parameters (.4.2) specify a DssVest stream running 17 June 2025 to 16 June 2029 with a cliff at 17 June 2026, "Vesting method: Linear per block with cliff," and — the operative line — **"Claim auth: Permissionless."**

Permissionless claim means the release of vested tokens requires no approval, no signature from a treasurer, and no multisig quorum. Anyone can call the claim; the tokens go to the designated recipient regardless of who triggers it.

This removes a specific and common lever. In a discretionary vesting arrangement, whoever must sign the release holds continuing power over the recipient long after the compensation was agreed — a slow-motion renegotiation available at every unlock. Making the claim permissionless converts vested compensation from something granted into something owed and automatically collectible, and it does so *at the contract level*, so the guarantee does not depend on the funder's continued good faith or continued existence.

It is a notably different posture from how Spark treats its Delegates and Risk Council, where compensation is administered by the Spark Foundation with explicit withholding and clawback rights. Contributors get a structural guarantee; governance participants get a discretionary one — the reverse of what independence considerations would suggest.

The alignment work is done instead by *time*: linear per-block accrual over four years with a twelve-month cliff means a contributor who leaves early forfeits the unvested remainder, which is a rule fixed in advance rather than a judgment made at the moment of departure.
description: A four-year linear schedule with a one-year cliff runs through DssVest with claim auth set to Permissionless, removing discretion over release from the entity funding it.
